newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia tin dealers not alarmed by LME price fall.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia tin dealers not alarmed by LME price fall.

text.p: Malaysian tin dealers said on Wednesday that they were not alarmed by the slump in London tin prices to 17-month lows saying the Kuala Lumpur Tin Market (KLTM) had shown encouraging signs of independence this year.
On Tuesday, three month LME tin retested Monday's 17-month low of $5,890 a tonne, a significant decline from the 1996 high of $6,650, and London chartists predicted further tumbles.
"There was a time when the KLTM was just following the LME (London Metal Exchange)," said a trader with a mining company in Kuala Lumpur.
"Now it has some strength of its own," he said, referring to recent weeks when Malaysian prices were up when the London market was down.
"On the 10-day average, the KLTM only follows the LME in five to six days now," he said.
Another dealer with a commodities house in Malaysia described the KLTM as "comatose", adding: "There doesn't really seem anything much to help the market although it's not dead."

The dealer, who also noted some independence in the Malaysian tin market this year, said it was still possible for the local price to climb back to the 15 ringgit ($6) a kg level by end of the year. The KLTM closed at 14.65 ringgit a kg on Wednesday.
"This used to be the support level until two months ago but now it seems to be the selling or profit-taking level," said the dealer.
